chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said:

I asked him face-to-face about a man who divorced his wife with two witnesses during her purity (period), then he traveled and testified to her return (raj'a). When he returned, he divorced her without sexual intercourse. I asked: Is that permissible for him? He said: Her divorce has become valid, because in these narrations there is no indication that he must divorce her as a 'divorce of the waiting period' (talaq al-'iddah). We only prevent him from divorcing her as a 'divorce of the waiting period'. As for the 'divorce of the Sunnah', there is no harm in him divorcing her after that, according to what was included in the narration of Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad and others. And the more preferred view indicating the permissibility of this is that it is permissible for him to divorce her with another divorce for the Sunnah, even if he did not have intercourse with her.

key_terms.طَلَاقَ الْعِدَّةِ: Divorce of the waiting period (specific legal category)
key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ: Divorce of the Sunnah (prophetic method of divorce)

ai.seo_question: Is a man allowed to divorce his wife without sexual intercourse if he already divorced her during her purity period?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of distinguishing between *Talaq al-Sunnah* (divorce during purity) and *Talaq al-'Iddah* (divorce during the waiting period), clarifying that the prohibition against divorcing without prior consummation applies specifically to the latter. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of the divorce and the subsequent waiting period, emphasizing that the Imam permits the second divorce even without intercourse because it is not classified as *Talaq al-'Iddah*. The narration highlights the nuanced application of the 'two witnesses' rule and the conditions under which a husband may exercise his right to divorce without the prerequisite of sexual union.
